acts.desc: Host Ira Glass goes with Ashli Lewis to a San Francisco psychic to find out if a longstanding prophecy about her is going to come true in 2010.
acts.label: Prologue
Act One
acts.desc: Shalom Auslander knows his next door neighbor will die in 2010. He's the author, most recently, of the memoir Foreskin's Lament.
acts.title: Chronicle Of A Death Foretold

acts.label: Act Two
acts.desc: Ira with teachers Shraddha Subramaniam and Samantha Cato, and their 2010 predictions for their sixth grade students at Intermediate School 303 in the Bronx, especially a student named Lewis de la Cruz.
acts.title: Lewis Time

acts.label: Act Three
acts.desc: Jonathan Menjivar has been thinking a lot about 2010 lately, especially about one upcoming event: The birth of his daughter. Jonathan's one of the producers of NPR's Fresh Air.
acts.title: Potus Operandi

acts.label: Act Four
acts.desc: When it comes to predictions, Etgar Keret only trusts one person in his family: His mom. She's amazingly accurate. So he asks her to clue him in about what the future of the mideast will be in 2010. Etgar's an Israeli writer; his latest book of short stories, translated into English, is The Girl on the Fridge.
acts.title: Nostra-mom-us

acts.label: Act Five
acts.desc: Adam Davidson and Alex Blumberg from our Planet Money team report on economic forecasts for 2010 and what they can and cannot accurately predict. Planet Money is a co-production of This American Life and NPR News.
acts.credits: By Alex Blumberg, Adam Davidson, Planet Money
acts.title: Funny You Don't Look Two-ish
